approach: Replace the single `checks` job in ci.yml with a `gate` job (D121 fingerprint, lookup, decide), parallel `fmt`, `clippy` and a 6-shard `test` matrix, a `pass` job that writes the D121 marker only when every check succeeded, and a final `ci` job (`if: always()`) that fails unless every needed job succeeded (or was skipped because the gate reused a pass). Add `xtask test-shard <k> <n> [--dry-run]` in xtask/src/shard.rs: it lists workspace test units from `cargo metadata --no-deps`, sorts them, gives unit i to shard i % n, and runs `cargo test --locked -p <pkg> <selector>` per unit. A new xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs reads ci.yml and checks the shards form an exact partition in three layers: a shape rule (matrix list and command), a pure `check_cover(shards, oracle)`, and an oracle built independently from cargo metadata and cross-checked against source files on disk by path (`src_path`), so renamed targets such as athena-cli's `[[bin]] name = "athena"` are handled. policy.rs and two doc strings under xtask/ are re-pointed at the new job names. No new crates (serde_json and regex are already xtask dependencies), so Cargo.lock stays unchanged.

decisions.choice: A separate `gate` job runs fingerprint, lookup and decide. fmt, clippy and test declare `needs: gate` and `if: needs.gate.outputs.skip != 'true'`. A separate `pass` job (default success() condition, needs gate, fmt, clippy, test) builds xtask, runs `ci-cache mark ci-pass` with an OUTCOME computed from the three results, and saves `ci-pass` with the gate's key.
decisions.reason: Fingerprint and lookup run once, not eight times. The marker is written only when every check succeeded, because a failed or skipped need skips `pass`. Mark and save steps carry no always()/failure(), as the existing policy test requires.

rejected.option: Run the whole D121 prelude in every job
rejected.why: Eight fingerprint builds, and eight jobs each deciding whether to write one marker, so a partial pass could be saved.

rejected.option: Put the marker step inside the ci job
rejected.why: ci would need a checkout and an xtask build before reporting.

rejected.option: Pass the xtask binary between jobs as an artifact
rejected.why: Needs extra action SHAs that cannot be verified here.

decisions.choice: The `ci` job needs [gate, fmt, clippy, test], runs `if: always()`, and a shell step reads needs.*.result. gate must be success. If gate.outputs.skip == 'true', fmt, clippy and test must all be skipped; otherwise all must be success. Anything else exits 1. ci does not need `pass`.
decisions.reason: One check name says whether a commit is green, including the reused-pass case. A cancelled job, or one skipped by mistake, cannot pass. A marker-write fault should not turn a commit red. The cost (ci can finish before pass writes the marker) is recorded as a known effect.

rejected.why: On a failed check pass is skipped, so ci needs special cases, and a marker-write failure would fail the required check.
A job skipped by a broken needs or if would pass silently.

decisions.choice: Shard unit = workspace test target. For each workspace member take targets with test:true and kind lib, rlib, proc-macro, bin or test, giving selectors --lib, --bin <name>, --test <name>. Add a --doc unit for each lib target with doctest:true. Sort by (package, selector); unit i goes to shard i % n; shards are 0-based.
decisions.reason: Mirrors what cargo test --workspace runs: examples and benches have test=false and are excluded; doctests run once per package. Deterministic with no cost data. Buy-first call recorded in a shard.rs comment: cargo metadata plus cargo test meet the need.

rejected.option: Shard by individual test name from `cargo test -- --list`
rejected.why: Compiles everything to plan; name filters can misselect on overlapping names.
More code and file-dependent split; a follow-up if the throughput review shows poor balance.
New pinned tool and changes how doctests run.

decisions.choice: test-shard runs one `cargo test --locked -p <pkg> <selector>` per unit, in order, keeps going after a failure, then exits non-zero naming the failed units. --dry-run prints one `<pkg> <selector>` line per unit and runs nothing. A comment in shard.rs and the risk list note that per-unit -p runs may resolve features differently from one --workspace run.
decisions.reason: Cargo cannot attach a different target selector to each -p, so one invocation per unit runs exactly the selected units. --dry-run gives the partition test and local users the selection without compiling.

rejected.why: Target flags apply to every selected package.

rejected.option: Group a shard's units by package
rejected.why: More code and does not remove the feature-resolution difference; follow-up if recompile cost shows.

decisions.choice: The partition test has three layers. (a) parse_workflow(text) -> Result<(Vec<u32>, u32), String> reads `shard: [..]` in the test job and the single `test-shard ${{ matrix.shard }} <n>` command by regex; requires the list to be exactly 0..n. (b) shard_units runs `xtask test-shard k n --dry-run` per listed k. (c) pure check_cover(shards, oracle) fails naming the unit if it is in two shards, in none, or in a shard but not in the oracle. check_partition(text) calls (a), (b), (c). Negatives: shape mutations of the ci.yml text test (a); cover-only cases call (c) directly with well-formed shards (unit removed, unit copied to a second shard, extra oracle unit, shard unit not in oracle), each asserted Err naming the unit; a positive control asserts Ok.
decisions.reason: Text mutations all change the matrix shape and are rejected before the cover comparison, so an always-Ok comparison would go unnoticed. A pure cover function can be fed well-formed but wrong shards. No YAML crate exists in Cargo.lock; regex is already a dev-dependency.

rejected.why: No mutation reaches the cover comparison.
Changes Cargo.lock and needs network for one fixed-shape matrix.

rejected.option: Use test-shard output as the oracle
rejected.why: Checks the splitter against itself.

decisions.choice: Answer to finding 2. The oracle is computed in ci_shards.rs from `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 --locked`, encoding cargo's documented target rules separately from shard.rs. It is cross-checked against the filesystem BY PATH, not by derived name: for each workspace member, every existing src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, src/bin/*.rs, src/bin/*/main.rs, tests/*.rs and tests/*/main.rs must equal the `src_path` of some metadata target (canonicalised), and that target's unit (--lib, --bin <metadata name>, --test <metadata name>) must be in the oracle. The old claim that the workspace has no target-name overrides is removed: crates/athena-cli/Cargo.toml declares [[bin]] name = "athena" path = "src/main.rs", and the path mapping yields `athena-cli --bin athena`, matching cargo. A file with no target, or whose target has test=false, fails with the path named.
decisions.reason: The check stays independent of the test/doctest flags and survives [[bin]]/[[test]] renames, so it passes on the real repository. Comment records why `cargo test --workspace --no-run` inside the test was rejected: it compiles the whole workspace and prints artifact paths, not stable target names.

rejected.option: Derive bin name from the package name
rejected.why: Wrong for athena-cli; the test would fail on the base commit.

rejected.option: Only comment on the shared rule
rejected.why: A comment documents the risk but detects nothing.

decisions.choice: Per-job target cache keys target-fmt-, target-clippy-, target-test- with the existing restore-key shape. The six test shards share one key; only shard 0 saves it, on the default branch only. Toolchain and registry keys and the default-branch-only save rule are unchanged. Answer to finding 3: the partial coverage of the saved test entry is recorded as a KNOWN EFFECT in the ci.yml comment, the CHANGELOG and ci-routing.md for the throughput review (the saved entry holds shard 0's packages and feature variants; other shards compile some of their packages cold). Single key kept.
decisions.reason: Different jobs build different artifacts, so one key would let them overwrite each other. Six shards saving one key race. The alternative, running `cargo test --workspace --no-run` before the save, would not help: it unifies features over the whole workspace, while the per-unit -p runs resolve per package, so the artifacts would not match the shards' builds, and it would lengthen the default-branch shard 0.

rejected.why: Six large entries against the repository cache quota.
Collisions between clippy and test artifacts.

rejected.option: Save after a workspace --no-run on shard 0
rejected.why: Different feature resolution than the shards use, so little reuse; extra time.

decisions.choice: Add timeout-minutes to every job, including the unchanged history, attribution and pr-head jobs. Values are ceilings (about 30 for fmt, clippy and each shard; smaller for gate, pass, ci), labelled as ceilings, not measurements.
decisions.reason: Criterion 1 requires it on every job; a timeout does not change what those jobs check.

rejected.option: Leave the three untouched jobs without a timeout
rejected.why: Violates criterion 1.

decisions.choice: Leave EARLY_RUN_JOB (crates/athena-core/src/gh/early.rs, 'fmt, clippy, tests') untouched. Record in the CHANGELOG and ci-routing.md, as a known effect, that land's early-run wait finds no check run with the old name and ends at once, so a landing run can miss the cached pass. The follow-up should name the job that writes the marker (`pass`), not `ci`, since ci can finish before the marker is saved.
decisions.reason: The crate and its test fixtures are outside the listed files; renaming to `ci` would still race the marker write.

rejected.option: Change the constant to ci here
rejected.why: Out of file scope, edits fixtures, still races pass.

rejected.option: Keep a job named 'fmt, clippy, tests'
rejected.why: Contradicts the requested single ci check name.

decisions.choice: Answer to finding 1. Modify xtask/tests/policy.rs only to re-point its two D121 tests from the single job to gate, the compute jobs and pass, replacing checks_job_steps() with job_steps(job_id). Keep both test function names unchanged because docs/decisions.md D121 (lines ~2987-2988) names them and the enforcement-map test checks names. The file sits under xtask/, which the request's Files line lists; the brief's expected-deliverables list omits it, so the reason is stated in the files list and the edit is limited to what the layout change forces (policy.rs lines ~523-529 find the job by `    name: fmt, clippy, tests` and end the slice at `\n  history:`).
decisions.reason: Without it `cargo test` fails on the new ci.yml (criterion 5). Re-pointing keeps the pass-marker enforcement (mechanism default).

rejected.why: Its tests fail on the new ci.yml.
Loses enforcement of the pass-marker rule.

Reword the reused-pass report string at xtask/src/ci_cache.rs:55 to name the gate job and the D121 layout (for example 'gate: reused an earlier pass; setup, build and checks skipped'), and update the module doc at ci_cache.rs:1, xtask/tests/fingerprint.rs:1 and xtask/src/main.rs:5. A grep found no test asserting the old string.
decisions.reason: After this change the job named 'fmt, clippy, tests' no longer exists, so the printed message and docs would be misleading. All are under xtask/.

rejected.why: The edit is a few strings in files already in scope and avoids a misleading log line.

risks.risk: The ci job could report green when a needed job was skipped or cancelled, or red on a legitimately reused pass.
risks.mitigation: workflow_jobs tests assert the step exits non-zero unless every need is success (or skipped when gate.skip is true), with text-mutation negatives.

risks.risk: The D121 marker could be written after a partial failure.
risks.mitigation: pass has the default success() condition and needs all four jobs; the policy test forbids always/failure/cancelled on mark and save steps; mark writes only for outcome success computed from all three results.

risks.risk: The shard split drops or repeats a target (doctests, a bin sharing a lib's name), or shard.rs and the oracle share a wrong belief about cargo's target rules, or a renamed target (athena-cli's `athena` bin) breaks the cross-check.
risks.mitigation: check_cover is a separate pure function with cover-only negatives; the oracle is written independently of shard.rs and cross-checked by src_path against files on disk, which handles [[bin]]/[[test]] renames; a source file with no test target fails loudly.

risks.risk: Per-unit `cargo test -p <pkg>` may resolve features differently from one `cargo test --workspace` (resolver unifies over selected packages), compiling extra dependency copies and running tests on a slightly different build.
risks.mitigation: Recorded in a shard.rs comment and the design doc for the throughput review; grouping by package is the follow-up.

risks.risk: The shared target-test- cache is saved by shard 0 only, so it holds shard 0's packages and feature variants; other shards compile some packages cold.
risks.mitigation: Stated as a known effect in ci.yml, CHANGELOG and ci-routing.md for the throughput review; single key kept to stay inside the cache quota.

risks.risk: Shards are unbalanced, or one failing shard masks others.
risks.mitigation: Each shard runs all its units before exiting non-zero and names failed ones; fail-fast: false keeps siblings running; balance follow-up recorded.

risks.risk: ci can go green before pass writes the marker, and land's early wait (stale EARLY_RUN_JOB) ends at once, so a landing run may miss the cached pass.
risks.mitigation: A miss costs one extra run; stated as a known effect with the follow-up naming the marker-writing job.

risks.risk: A too-short timeout-minutes fails a legitimate cold run.
risks.mitigation: Ceilings of about 30 minutes for compute jobs versus the D125 whole-run baseline of about 16; labelled as ceilings, to be reviewed by the throughput review.

risks.risk: New per-job target cache keys start cold, so the first runs after merge are slower.
risks.mitigation: Comments and the design note say so.

risks.risk: Editing policy.rs, ci_cache.rs and fingerprint.rs goes beyond the brief's deliverable list.
risks.mitigation: All are under xtask/, which the request lists; edits are limited to what the layout change forces (policy tests, a log string and doc comments); assertions are kept, not weakened.

demonstrations.method: Tests `workflow_jobs_*` in xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs read the real ci.yml with std::fs, split it into job blocks (two-space-indent keys under `jobs:`) and assert: jobs fmt, clippy, test exist; test has strategy.matrix.shard of 6 entries; the job with `name: ci` has needs containing gate, fmt, clippy, test, has `if: always()`, and its run step exits 1 unless each need is success (or skipped when gate.outputs.skip == 'true'); every job block has timeout-minutes. Text mutations (remove `if: always()`, drop one needs entry, strip one timeout-minutes) are asserted to be rejected.
demonstrations.observes: Tests pass on the new ci.yml; each mutated copy is rejected with a message naming the missing item.
demonstrations.fails_without: If ci.yml lacked the separate jobs, the 6-shard matrix, the ci job's needs / if: always() / result check, or any job's timeout-minutes, one of these tests fails.
demonstrations.seam: Reads the real .github/workflows/ci.yml via std::fs with line regexes over job blocks; no double; same style as existing checks_job_steps in xtask/tests/policy.rs (exists). The new test file is added by plan step 6.

demonstrations.method: Re-pointed D121 tests in policy.rs use job_steps(job_id). In gate: fingerprint < lookup < decide, lookup is cache/restore keyed by the fingerprint. Each compute job has `needs: gate` and the skip condition, and restores toolchain, registry and target caches. `pass` needs gate, fmt, clippy, test, has no always/failure/cancelled, runs ci-cache mark then cache/save of ci-pass with no default-branch condition. Shared-cache saves stay default-branch-only. In ci_shards.rs, `workflow_actions_are_pinned` asserts every `uses:` matches @[0-9a-f]{40}, and `workflow_caches` asserts the three cache restores in fmt, clippy and test.

demonstrations.observes: All pass; existing policy assertions are kept, moved to the job that now holds each step.
demonstrations.fails_without: An unpinned uses, a removed cache layer, dropped gate/lookup/mark steps, or always() / a default-branch condition on the mark or save step makes the pinned-actions test or the re-pointed policy tests fail.

demonstrations.method: Test `shards_in_ci_yml_partition_every_workspace_test_target` calls check_partition(real ci.yml text): parse the matrix list and n, run the built `xtask test-shard k n --dry-run` for each listed k, then check_cover against the independent cargo-metadata oracle; expect Ok. Negatives, each asserted Err: (a) shape mutations of the ci.yml text (drop shard 5 with n=6; duplicate a shard; change the command's n to 5), each asserted to differ from the original; (b) cover-only cases calling check_cover directly with real per-shard unit sets: a unit removed (error names it missing), a unit copied into a second shard (error names it duplicated), an oracle with one extra synthetic unit, a shard unit absent from the oracle. A positive control checks check_cover returns Ok for the unmodified sets.
demonstrations.observes: The positive test passes on the repository's ci.yml; each negative passes because it is rejected, the cover-only ones by check_cover with the unit named.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the cover comparison always returned Ok, the cover-only negatives fail; if the shape rule were missing, the text-mutation cases fail; if the real shards missed or repeated a unit, the positive test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: the built xtask binary, `test-shard <k> <n> --dry-run`, via env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_xtask") (pattern in xtask/tests/fingerprint.rs, exists). Fixtures: the real ci.yml, in-memory mutated strings, and shard/oracle sets passed as arguments to the pure check_cover (step 6). The oracle is the test's own cargo metadata call plus the by-path filesystem cross-check, with no logic imported from shard.rs. The subcommand and --dry-run are added by steps 2-4.

demonstrations.method: In ci_shards.rs, `test_shard_6_is_disjoint_and_equals_the_workspace_target_set` runs test-shard k 6 --dry-run for k in 0..=5 and asserts the unit lines are pairwise disjoint and their union equals the oracle; `test_shard_1_equals_the_workspace` does the same for n=1; `oracle_matches_files_on_disk` maps every src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, src/bin/*.rs and tests/*.rs (and */main.rs) of each member to a metadata target by src_path and requires its unit in the oracle (passes for athena-cli's renamed bin `athena`); `test_shard_rejects_bad_arguments` runs `6 6`, `0 0`, `3 2`, `x 6` and no arguments and asserts non-zero exit and an error message. Unit tests in shard.rs feed a hand-written metadata JSON to plan_units: examples and benches excluded; bin/test targets get --bin/--test; a lib with doctest=false has no --doc unit; select over n=1, 6 and n > unit count is disjoint and complete.
demonstrations.observes: All xtask tests pass, including existing ones. `cargo run -p xtask -- test-shard 0 6 --dry-run` prints a stable sorted list, and the six shards together equal the workspace target set.
demonstrations.fails_without: If test-shard were missing, overlapped, dropped any unit (for example doctests), or accepted k>=n or n=0, the disjoint/union and bad-argument tests fail. If a target were renamed in a way the oracle mishandles, oracle_matches_files_on_disk fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: the xtask binary (main dispatch to shard::command) run via CARGO_BIN_EXE_xtask against the real workspace. For unit tests, shard::plan_units(&serde_json::Value) takes the metadata JSON as an argument so a fixture is injected. Both added by steps 2-4; integration tests by step 6.

open_questions: EARLY_RUN_JOB in crates/athena-core/src/gh/early.rs is 'fmt, clippy, tests'. After this change land's early wait finds no such check run and ends at once. Do the maintainers want it pointed at `pass` (or ci made to wait for pass) in this job? The plan leaves it out and records it as a known effect.
Branch protection must change from the old check name to `ci`; this is outside the repository, so the changelog states it.

Every compute job runs ./setup.sh --ci, which builds xtask and athena in release mode. The code does not show whether fmt and clippy need it; kept for fidelity and the existing cache; the throughput review can judge.
Index-modulo over target units can leave shards unbalanced (one crate's tests cannot be split). Weighting by source size is a possible follow-up once real shard times exist.
ci.yml's matrix list and test-shard command shape are fixed by the regex parser. A later move to include or fromJSON makes the test fail loudly and the parser must be updated.
Whether the policy.rs edit is accepted as in scope (it is under xtask/ but absent from the brief's deliverable list).
